overview: This Senate resolution designates December 6, 2025, as 'National Miners Day' to honor the work and sacrifices of American miners. December 6 is the anniversary of the 1907 mine disaster in Monongah, West Virginia, which the resolution describes as the deadliest industrial accident in U.S. history and a turning point in the push for mine safety and health protections. The resolution encourages Americans to take part in local and national activities honoring miners. It is ceremonial and does not change any law. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on December 11, 2025.
for: Supporters say miners have long done dangerous work that helped build the country, and that remembering disasters like Monongah keeps attention on worker safety.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law, safety rule, or spending.
